sets.s: Let’s use the biggest paintbrushes to paint these walls as it will get the job done faster.
i: The biggest paintbrushes are accessible to use to paint the walls.
M
The statement works only if are readily available to use, whether they are the biggest paintbrushes or not. Therefore, an assumption must be made.
There is enough paint to cover the walls.
N
The assumption states that there is enough paint to cover the walls, though there is no mention of that fact in the statement. Therefore, an assumption has not been made.
Using the smallest paintbrushes would mean that the job would never get completed.
N

The assumption implies that the larger the brush, the faster the job, so the smaller the brush, the slower the job. Though this may at first appear to be a contraposition and is a fallacy of deductive reasoning, if the statement suggests that larger = quicker, it is fair to deduce that smaller = slower. However, it is not necessary to assume this in order to make the statement. Therefore, an assumption is not made here.

sets.s: You’ll definitely need to have warm clothing for this journey.
i: At least a part of the journey will be somewhere requiring warm clothing.
M
The statement relies on the fact that warm clothing is needed which implies there will be at least some cold sections of the journey.
The journey will be easier with warm clothing.
N
The statement says warm clothing will be needed, we cannot assume the ease of the journey is dependent on the clothing.
The person listening to this has warm clothing.
N
They are being advised to wear warm clothing for the journey. This does not imply that the recipient of this actually has warm clothing to wear.

sets.s: Using a calculator would make the test a lot easier.
i: The test will be completed more quickly if a calculator is used.
N
The statement says the test will be easier. It does not suggest that it will speed things up.
Anyone taking the test has access to a calculator.
N
The statement suggests that using a calculator would make things easier, but not that everyone has access to a calculator.
There are ways to make the test easier.
M
It is necessary to assume that the test can be made easier if using a calculator to do so is a suggested idea.

sets.s: I was charged 40p for every minute I was on the telephone, which came as somewhat of a surprise to me.
i: The phone call was made by the person who was charged.
N
The statement only tells us they were on the line, so is it not justified to assume that this person made the call. This assumption is not made within the statement.
The person involved in this phone call was only charged for every full minute they were on the line.
N
The passage never hints towards whether the charge is for every full minute or not. They could have been charged for a fraction of a minute (20p for 30 seconds).
The person on the line was unsure of how much they were going to be charged.
M
The statement suggests that they knew there was a charge but were unsure on how much. ‘Somewhat of a surprise’ suggests that the participant did not expect to be charged 40 pence a minute.
